inputs.mid_cycle_fcf_note: last_fcf ($10,200M) is a normalized mid-cycle base-year FCF, NOT reported Q1-2026 FCF ($5,094M, inflated by the $2.8B WBD termination fee) or FY2026 guidance (~$12.5B, which nets the fee benefit against the associated Q2-2026 cash tax drag). FY2025 actual FCF was $9,461M; the normalized base assumes an underlying uplift off that base, stripped of one-off distortions.
inputs.shares_outstanding_note: Post 10-for-1 split (Nov 2025). Q1-2026 diluted weighted avg was 4,298M; reduced to 4,250M to reflect record ~$4.7B of Q2-2026 buybacks.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1-2026 balance sheet: total debt $14,360M minus cash $12,260M = ~$2,100M. Grossed up to ~$5,000M (conservative) to reflect ~$4.7B of Q2-2026 cash spent on buybacks, which depleted the cash balance while debt remained roughly unchanged.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (9.9%) diverges over 100% from EPS 5yr CAGR (33.0%), and raw FCF CAGRs (37.5% 5yr / 77.6% 3yr) are not meaningful because they compound off a depressed FY2020/FY2022 FCF trough caused by content-spend timing (near-zero cash FCF in those years), mechanically inflating the CAGR. Equity CAGR is also buyback-distorted (similar to Visa) since Netflix has aggressively repurchased shares (record $4.7B in Q2-2026 alone), suppressing book equity growth relative to true value creation. Given these distortions, revenue CAGR (approximately 12.6%, stable and consistent across both 3yr/5yr windows) is used as the primary anchor for Year-1 FCF growth in the base case rather than equity or raw FCF CAGRs.

base.notes: FCF growth starts near revenue-CAGR-consistent 12%, decelerating to 6% by Year 5, in line with Q3-2026 guided deceleration (11.7% YoY) and margin normalization post FY2026 guide (31.5% operating margin, ad revenue ~$3B doubling).

bull.notes: Ad business scales well beyond the $3B FY2026 target (doubles again in later years), continued pricing power, live sports/content flywheel sustains higher growth; margin expansion continues past the 31.5% FY2026 guide.

bear.notes: Growth deceleration seen in the Q3-2026 guide (11.7%) worsens further amid the combined Paramount-WBD competitive threat and Amazon Prime Video near-parity in US share; content cost inflation compresses margins; multiple compression risk as growth normalizes toward low-single-digits.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.note: FY2016-FY2020 hypergrowth-era multiples (P/E 78-288x) treated as outliers; the mature-era 2021+ window is the meaningful anchor. All multiples computed on post-split basis at FY-end (Dec) closing prices.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied multiples from base-case IV ($47.51) sit far BELOW historical trading ranges (implied P/E 18.8x vs 2021+ avg 41x; implied P/B 7.8x vs 10yr avg 14.5x). The DCF is conservative relative to how the market has ever priced NFLX; the gap to the current price reflects the market's premium growth multiple, not aggressive model assumptions.
sanity_check.base_year_note: Base-year FCF was pre-normalized to $10,200M (mid-cycle) before the DCF ran, stripping the one-off $2.8B WBD termination fee received in Q1-2026 and its Q2-2026 cash-tax drag, so peak-earnings extrapolation was avoided by construction.

valuation_philosophy: Conservative cash-flow anchor for a premium-multiple growth stock. Netflix has never traded at multiples a 9.5%-WACC/3%-terminal-growth DCF can justify (implied terminal ~16x FCF vs the 30-45x P/E the market has paid since 2022), so negative headline upside is expected from this model and does not by itself mean the stock must fall. The DCF instead marks the price at which an investor underwrites a 15% CAGR with little reliance on multiple persistence (entry price ~$28.7). Base-year FCF is normalized to $10.2B: reported Q1-2026 FCF ($5.1B) was inflated by the $2.8B Warner Bros. Discovery deal-termination fee Netflix received, and Q2-2026 FCF ($1.5B) was depressed by cash taxes on that fee; FY2026 management guidance is ~$12.5B including the fee. Growth anchors to the stable ~12.6% revenue CAGR rather than the buyback-distorted equity CAGR or trough-inflated FCF CAGR.
